patch.final: on a un foncteur en \inserted{le triple} $(\deleted{Z}\inserted{T}\longrightarrow X_{\unsure{0|\bullet}}\longrightarrow Y)$
patch.evidence: The baseline begins with separate groups on, a, and un, then the long f stem and connected letters of foncteur, followed by en. Above the gap after en are le and triple, including a long p descender and final l/e strokes. They attach to the following parenthesized triple. The first T of that triple again overwrites a diagonal Z. Its following shaft has a short terminal hook. The second arrow has a much heavier, retraced head; no second independently spaced arrowhead is proposed. Independent audit additionally records the small dark subscript-like loop below X; see the separate audit_b08_index row.

changes_append.place: main line 7, small mark below/right of X in the parenthesized triple
changes_append.evidence: The independent audit exposed a compact dark loop with a small terminal return, in subscript position below/right of X. It is as dark as the foreground lettering and is retained as a doubtful zero/point. Its identity is not secured and no mathematical definition for an indexed X is supplied by this passage. The whole triple was inspected in b08 and the open mark in the listed focus.

doubts_append.place: main line 7, subscript-like mark on X in the triple
doubts_append.alternatives: Small loop 0; point/bullet-like mark. The role of this dark foreground mark is not established.
connexes; connexe. Compressed final e/s strokes remain unresolved.

patch.first_words_or_objects: on a un foncteur en ... (T to X with doubtful 0/bullet subscript to Y) variable. En particulier:

notes_append: Independent audit: a dark small loop in subscript position on X in the parenthesized triple was absent from both drafts and the first reading. It is now transcribed as an uncertain 0/point. No indexed X is defined here; the surrounding unindexed triples do not justify erasing the visible mark or declaring a mathematical correction. The 0-connexes/connexe ending remains explicitly open. The formula (11) blackening does not establish two separate alphabetic layers.
